newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ markets won't open for post-election Sunday.
newsitem.headline: NZ markets won't open for post-election Sunday.

text.p: The New Zealand Financial Markets Association said on Friday it had not and was not moving to set up any unofficial or official market on Sunday, the day after the general election.
The association said this was contrary to "certain articles appearing in the media".

The NZFMAI said it had not sought to sanction any interbank or other market activity in NZD foreign exchange, debt securities or derivatives outside normal interbank trading hours. It emphasised the normal market conventions in terms of trading ranges should apply.

It said it had received assurances from banks and brokers operating in New Zealand financial markets that there was no intention to operate an interbank market on Sunday, either officially or unofficially.
"Accordingly it would be inappropriate for NZD foreign exchange or interest rates appearing on multi-contributor information services to be updated from Friday's close until Monday morning," it said.

The NZFMAI suggested members be vigilant in terms of clarity of arrangements in respect of option products, for example knock in/knock out structures, and stop loss/take profit orders with respect to conventions regarding trading ranges.
